q: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank from empty to full in 30 minutes, 20 minutes, and 10 minutes respectively. When the tank is empty, all the three pipes are opened. A, B and C discharge chemical solutions P, Q and R respectively. What is the proportion of the solution R in the liquid in the tank after 3 minutes?
s: Part filled by (A + B + C) in 3 minutes $$\begin{aligned} & = 3\left( {\frac{1}{{30}} + \frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{10}}} \right) \\ & = {3 \times \frac{{11}}{{60}}} = \frac{{11}}{{20}} \\ & {\text{Part}}\,{\text{filled}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{C}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{3}}\,{\text{minutes}} = \frac{3}{{10}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{ratio}} \\ & = {\frac{3}{{10}} \times \frac{{20}}{{11}}} = \frac{6}{{11}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 5 and 6 hours respectively. Pipe C can empty it in 12 hours. If all the three pipes are opened together, then the tank will be filled in:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Net}}\,{\text{part}}\,{\text{filled}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{hour}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{{12}}} = \frac{{17}}{{60}} \\ & \therefore {\text{The}}\,{\text{tank}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{full}}\,{\text{in}}\,\frac{{60}}{{17}}\,{\text{hours}} \\ & i.e.,\,3\frac{9}{{17}}\,{\text{hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A pump can fill a tank with water in 2 hours. Because of a leak, it took $$2\frac{1}{3}$$ hours to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water of the tank in:
s: Work done by the leak in 1 hour $$\begin{aligned} & = {\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{7}} = \frac{1}{{14}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Leak will empty the tank in 14 hours

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in $$37\frac{1}{2}$$ minutes and 45 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened. The cistern will be filled in just half an hour, if the B is turned off after:
s: Let B be turned off after x minutes. Then, Part filled by (A + B) in x min. + Part filled by A in (30 - x) min. = 1 $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore x\left( {\frac{2}{{75}} + \frac{1}{{45}}} \right) + \left( {30 - x} \right).\frac{2}{{75}} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{11x}}{{225}} + \frac{{ {60 - 2x} }}{{75}} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow 11x + 180 - 6x = 225 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 9 \end{aligned}$$

q: A tank is filled by three pipes with uniform flow. The first two pipes operating simultaneously fill the tank in the same time during which the tank is filled by the third pipe alone. The second pipe fills the tank 5 hours faster than the first pipe and 4 hours slower than the third pipe. The time required by the first pipe is:
s: Suppose, first pipe alone takes x hours to fill the tank. Then, Second and third pipes will take (x - 5) and (x - 9) hours respectively to fill the tank. $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{{ {x - 5} }} = \frac{1}{{ {x - 9} }} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{x - 5 + x}}{{x\left( {x - 5} \right)}} = \frac{1}{{ {x - 9} }} \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {2x - 5} \right)\left( {x - 9} \right) = x\left( {x - 5} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} - 18x + 45 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x - 15} \right)\left( {x - 3} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 15{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} \left[ {{\text{neglecting}}\,x = 3} \right] \end{aligned}$$

q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 24 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 15 minutes. The capacity of the tank is:
s: Work done by the waste pipe in 1 minute $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{{15}} - \left( {\frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{24}}} \right) \\ & = {\frac{1}{{15}} - \frac{{11}}{{120}}} \\ & = - \frac{1}{{40}}\,\,\,\,\,\left[ { - ve\,{\text{sign}}\,{\text{means}}\,{\text{emptying}}} \right] \\ & \therefore {\text{Volume}}\,{\text{of}}\,\frac{1}{{40}}{\text{part}} = 3\,{\text{gallons}} \\ & {\text{Volume}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{whole}} \\ & = \left( {3 \times 40} \right){\text{gallons}} \\ & = 120\,{\text{gallons}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A tank is filled in 5 hours by three pipes A, B and C. The pipe C is twice as fast as B and B is twice as fast as A. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
s: Suppose pipe A alone takes x hours to fill the tank. Then, pipes B and C will take $$\frac{x}{2}$$ and $$\frac{x}{4}$$ hours respectively to fill the tank. $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{x} + \frac{2}{x} + \frac{4}{x} = \frac{1}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{7}{x} = \frac{1}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 35\,{\text{hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 4 hours. Had they been opened separately, then B would have taken 6 hours more than A to fill the cistern. How much time will be taken by A to fill the cistern separately?
s: Let the cistern be filled by pipe A alone in x hours. Then, pipe B will fill it in (x + 6) hours $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{{ {x + 6} }} = \frac{1}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{x + 6 + x}}{{x\left( {x + 6} \right)}} = \frac{1}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} - 2x - 24 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x - 6} \right)\left( {x + 4} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 6\,{\kern 1pt} {\kern 1pt} \left[ {{\text{neglecting the negative value of }}x} \right] \end{aligned}$$

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. If both the pipes are used together, then how long will it take to fill the tank?
s: Part filled by A in 1 minute = $$\frac{1}{{20}}$$ Part filled by B in 1 minute = $$\frac{1}{{30}}$$ Part filled by (A + B) in 1 minute $$\begin{aligned} & = {\frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{30}}} = \frac{1}{{12}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Both pipes can fill the tank in 12 minutes

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 minutes and 20 minutes respectively. Both the pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe A is turned off. What is the total time required to fill the tank?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Part}}\,{\text{filled}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{4}}\,{\text{minutes}} \\ & = 4\left( {\frac{1}{{15}} + \frac{1}{{20}}} \right) = \frac{7}{{15}} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{part}} = {1 - \frac{7}{{15}}} = \frac{8}{{15}} \\ & {\text{Part}}\,{\text{filled}}\,{\text{by}}\,B\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{minute}} = \frac{1}{{20}} \\ & \therefore \frac{1}{{20}}:\frac{8}{{15}}::1:x \\ & x = {\frac{8}{{15}} \times 1 \times 20} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = 10\frac{2}{3}\,\min \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = 10\min .\,40\,\sec . \\ & \therefore {\text{The}}\,{\text{tank}}\,{\text{will}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{full}}\,{\text{in}}\, \\ & = {4\min . + 10\min . +\, 40\sec .} \\ & = 14\min .\,40\sec . \end{aligned}$$

q: One pipe can fill a tank three times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 36 minutes, then the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in:
s: Let the slower pipe alone fill the tank in x minutes. Then, faster pipe will fill it in $$\frac{x}{3}$$ minutes. $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{x} + \frac{3}{x} = \frac{1}{{36}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{4}{x} = \frac{1}{{36}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 144\,\text{minutes} \end{aligned}$$

q: A large tanker can be filled by two pipes A and B in 60 minutes and 40 minutes respectively. How many minutes will it take to fill the tanker from empty state if B is used for half the time and A and B fill it together for the other half?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Part}}\,{\text{filled}}\,{\text{by}}\,(A + B)\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{minute}} \\ & = {\frac{1}{{60}} + \frac{1}{{40}}} = \frac{1}{{24}} \\ & {\text{Suppose}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{tank}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{filled}}\,{\text{in}}\,x\,{\text{minutes}} \\ & {\text{Then}},\,\frac{x}{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{24}} + \frac{1}{{40}}} \right) = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{2} \times \frac{1}{{15}} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 30\,\text{minutes} \end{aligned}$$

q: A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
s: Time taken by one tap to fill half of the the tank = 3 hours Part filled by the four taps in 1 hour $$\begin{aligned} & = {4 \times \frac{1}{6}} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & {\text{Remaining}}\,{\text{part}} = {1 - \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & \therefore \frac{2}{3}:\frac{1}{2}::1:x \\ & \Rightarrow x = {\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times \frac{3}{2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{3}{4}\,hrs.\,\,i.e.,\,45\,\operatorname{mins} . \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{total}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{taken}} = 3\,hrs.\,45\,mins. \end{aligned}$$

q: Three taps A, B and C can fill a tank in 12, 15 and 20 hours respectively. If A is open all the time and B and C are open for one hour each alternately, the tank will be full in:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {{\text{A + B}}} \right){\text{'s 1 hour work}} \\ & {\text{ = }} {\frac{1}{{12}} + \frac{1}{{15}}} = \frac{9}{{60}} = \frac{3}{{20}} \\ & \left( {{\text{A + C}}} \right){\text{'s 1 hour work}} \\ & {\text{ = }} {\frac{1}{{12}} + \frac{1}{{20}}} = \frac{8}{{60}} = \frac{2}{{15}} \\ & {\text{Part filled in 2 hrs}} \\ & {\text{ = }} {\frac{3}{{20}} + \frac{2}{{15}}} = \frac{{17}}{{60}} \\ & {\text{Part filled in 6 hrs}} \\ & {\text{ = }} {3 \times \frac{{17}}{{60}}} = \frac{{17}}{{20}} \\ & {\text{Remaining part}} \\ & {\text{ = }} {1 - \frac{{17}}{{20}}} = \frac{3}{{20}} \end{aligned}$$ Now it is the turn of A and B and $$\frac{3}{{20}}$$ part is filled by A and B in 1 hour ∴ Total time taken to fill tank = (6 + 1) hrs = 7 hrs

q: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 6 hours. After working at it together for 2 hours, C is closed and A and B can fill the remaining part in 7 hours. The number of hours taken by C alone to fill the tank is:
s: Part filled in 2 hours = $$\frac{2}{6}$$ = $$\frac{1}{3}$$ Remaining part = $${1 - \frac{1}{3}}$$ = $$\frac{2}{3}$$ ∴ (A + B)'s 7 hour's work = $$\frac{2}{3}$$ (A + B)'s 1 hour's work = $$\frac{2}{{21}}$$ ∴ C's 1 hour's work = {(A + B + C)'s 1 hour's work} - {(A + B's 1 hour's work} $$\begin{aligned} & = {\frac{1}{6} - \frac{2}{{21}}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{14}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ C alone can fill the tank in 14 hours

q: Water is continuously supplied from a reservoir to a locality at the steady rate of 10000 liters per hours. When delivery exceeds demand the excess water is stored in a tank. If the demand for 8 consecutive three hour periods is 10000, 10000, 45000, 25000, 40000, 15000, 60000 and 35000 liters respectively, what will be the minimum capacity required of the water tank (in thousand liters)to meet the demand and avoid any wastage?
A pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another pipe can empty it in y (y > x) hours. If both pipes are open, in how many hours will the tank is filled?
s: Net part filled in 1 hour $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{= }}\left( {\frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{y}} \right) \\ & = \left( {\frac{{y - x}}{{xy}}} \right) \end{aligned}$$ ∴ The tank will be filled in $$= \left( {\frac{{xy}}{{y - x}}} \right)\,\,{\text{hours}}$$

q: A pipe can fill a tank with water in 3 hours. Due to leakage in bottom, it takes $$3\frac{1}{2}$$ hours to fill it. In what time the leak will empty the completely filled tank?
s: Let the total capacity of tank is 21 units A's efficiency is 7 units/hr A's efficiency after leakage 6 units/hr leakage efficiency = 7 - 6 = 1 unit/hr leakage will empty the filled tank $$\frac{{{\text{Total Capacity}}}}{{{\text{Efficiency }}}} = \frac{{21}}{1}$$ = 21hours

q: Two pipe can fill a cistern in 3 hours and 4 hours respectively and a waste pipe can empty it in 2 hours. If all the three pipes are kept open, then the cistern will be filled in-
s: Part of the cistern filled in 1 hour $$= \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{2}$$ (Cistern filled by 1 st pipe + Cistern filled by 2 nd pipe – Cistern emptied by 3 rd pipe ) $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{4 + 3 - 6}}{{12}} \\ & = \frac{1}{{12}} \end{aligned}$$ Hence, the cistern will be filled in 12 hours.

q: $$\frac{3}{4}$$ part of the tank is full of water. When 30 litres of water is taken out, the tank becomes empty. The capacity of the tank is -
s: If tank has 4x liters of total capacity and its holds 3x liters of water and if 30 liters of water is taken out, then tank becomes empty. It means 3x liters of water is taken out 3x = 30 liters x = 10 liters Capacity of tank = 4x = 4 × 10 = 40 liters

q: A tank with capacity T liters is empty. If water flows into the tank from pipe X at the rate of x liters per minute and water is pumped out by Y at the rate of y liters per minute and x > y, then how many minutes will the tank be filled?
s: Net volume filled in 1 minute = (x - y) liters ∴ The tank will be filled in = $$\frac{{\text{T}}}{{\left( {x - y} \right)}}$$ minutes

q: A pipe can fill a tank in 3 hours. There are two outlet pipes from the tank which can empty it in 7 and 10 hours respectively. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the tank will be filled in -
s: Net part filled in 1 hour $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\frac{1}{3} - \left( {\frac{1}{7} + \frac{1}{{10}}} \right) \\ & = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{{17}}{{70}} \\ & = \frac{{19}}{{210}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ The tank will be filled in $$\frac{{210}}{{19}}$$ hours i.e. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{= 11}}\frac{1}{{19}}{\text{ hours}} \\ & \cong 11\,{\text{hours }} \end{aligned}$$

q: A vessel has three pipes connected to it , two to supply liquid and one to draw liquid. The first alone can fill the vessel in $$4\frac{1}{2}$$ hours, the second in 3 hours and the third can empty it in $$1\frac{1}{2}$$ hours. If all the pipes are opened simultaneously when the vessel is half full, how soon will it be emptied?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Net part filled in 1 hour}} \\ & = \frac{2}{3} - \left( {\frac{2}{9} + \frac{1}{3}} \right) \\ & = \left( {\frac{2}{3} - \frac{5}{9}} \right) \\ & = \frac{1}{9} \\ & \therefore \,\frac{1}{9}\,:\,\frac{1}{2}\,::\,1\,:\,x \\ & {\text{or}}\,\,\,x = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 9} \right) = 4\frac{1}{2}{\text{ hours}} \\ & {\text{So, the tank will be emptied in}} \\ & {\text{ = }}4\frac{1}{2}{\text{ hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two pipe A and B can fill a water tank in 20 and 24 minutes respectively and a third pipe C can empty at the rate of 3 gallons per minute. If A, B and C are open together to fill the tank in 15 minutes, find the capacity of tank?
s: Work done by the C pipe in 1 minute $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{{15}} - \left( {\frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{24}}} \right) \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{{15}} - \frac{{11}}{{120}}} \right) \\ & = - \frac{1}{{40}}\,\left[ { - {\text{ve}}\,{\text{means}}\,{\text{emptying}}} \right] \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Volume of $$\frac{1}{{40}}$$ part = 3 gallons. Volume of whole = (3 × 40) gallons = 120 gallons.

q: Three pipes P, Q and R can separately fill a cistern in 4, 8 and 12 hours respectively. Another pipe S can empty the completely filled cistern in 10 hours. Which of the following arrangements will fill the empty cistern in less time than others?
o: P, R and S are open
P, Q and S are open
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{(Total Capacity)}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{120}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\overline { \downarrow \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \downarrow \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \downarrow \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \downarrow } \\ & {\text{efficiency 30}}\,\,\,\,\,\,15\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,10\,\,\, - 12 \\ & {\text{hours}} \to \,\,\mathop 4\limits_{\left( {\text{P}} \right)}^ \downarrow \,\,\,\,\,\,\mathop 8\limits_{\left( {\text{Q}} \right)}^ \downarrow \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\mathop {12}\limits_{\left( {\text{R}} \right)}^ \downarrow \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\mathop {10}\limits_{\left( {\text{S}} \right)}^ \downarrow \end{aligned}$$ In order to fill the cistern in less time. So, efficiency of filling should be more now, check all options (A) → Q efficiency 15 units/hr (B) → (P + R - S) efficiency = 30 + 10 - 12 = 28 units/hr (C) → (P - S) efficiency = 30 - 12 = 18 units/hr (D) → (P + Q - S) efficiency = 30 + 15 - 12 = 33 units/hr Option (D) is answer Since efficiency of option (D) is highest

q: A tank has a leak which would empty the completely filled tank in 10 hours. If the tank is full of water and a tap is opened which admits 4 litres of water per minute in the tank , the leak takes 15 hours to empty the tank. How many litres of water does the tank hold?
s: Let the total capacity of the tank is 30 units. The efficiency of Leakage(Pipe A) will be $$\frac{30}{10}$$ = 3 And the efficiency of the leakage (Pipe A) and another Pipe (B) which is filling the tank will be $$\frac{30}{15}$$ = 2 Pipe A is emptying at 3 units/hr and when filling pipe B started then the emptying rate will come down to 2 units/hr. ∴ Filling Pipe B efficiency is 3 - 2 = 1unit/hr Pipe B will be fill the tank in $$\frac{30}{1}$$ = 30 hrs Filling rate of Pipe B per minute is 4 litter ∴ Total Capacity of tank will be = (4 × 60) × 30 = 7200 litters

q: A pump can fill a tank with water in 2 hours. Because of a leak, it took $$2\frac{1}{3}$$ hours to to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water of the tank in?
s: Work done by the leak in 1 hour $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{7}} \right) = \frac{1}{{14}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Leak will empty the tank in 14 hours

q: One pipe can fill a tank three times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 36 minutes, then the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in-
s: Let the slower pipe alone fill the tank in x minutes Then, Faster pipe alone will fill it in $$\frac{x}{3}$$ minutes $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{x} + \frac{3}{x} = \frac{1}{{36}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{4}{x} = \frac{1}{{36}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 144 \end{aligned}$$ So slower pipe alone will fill the tank in 144 min.

q: A swimming pool is filled by three pipes with uniform flow. The first two pipes operating simultaneously fill the pool in the same time during which the pool is filled by the third pipe alone. The second pipe fills the pool 5 hours faster than the first pipe and 4 hours slower than the third pipe. The time required by the first pipe is?
s: Suppose first pipe alone takes x hours to fill the tank. Then second and third pipes will takes (x - 5) and (x - 9) hours respectively to fill the tank. $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{{\left( {x - 5} \right)}} = \frac{1}{{\left( {x - 9} \right)}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{x - 5 + x}}{{x\left( {x - 5} \right)}} = \frac{1}{{\left( {x - 9} \right)}} \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {2x - 5} \right)\left( {x - 9} \right) = x\left( {x - 5} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} - 18x + 45 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x - 15} \right)\left( {x - 3} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 15\left[ {{\text{neglecting }}x\,{\text{ = 3}}} \right] \end{aligned}$$ So, first pipe alone takes 15 hrs to fill the tank.

q: 12 buckets of water fill a tank when the capacity of each bucket is 13.5 litres. How many buckets will be needed to fill the same tank, if the capacity of each bucket is 9 litres?
s: Capacity of the tank = (12 × 13.5) litres = 162 litres Capacity of each bucket = 9 litres Number of buckets needed $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{= }}\left( {\frac{{162}}{9}} \right) \\ & = 18 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 hours respectively. Both the pipes are opened to fill the tank but when the tank is one - third full, a leak develops in the tank through which one - third water supplied by both the pipes gose out. The total time taken to fill the tank is?
s: Part filled by (A + B) in 1 hour $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{= }}\left( {\frac{1}{{20}} + \frac{1}{{30}}} \right) \\ & = \frac{1}{{12}} \end{aligned}$$ So, A and B together can fill the tank in 12 hrs, $$\frac{1}{3}$$ part is filled by (A + B) in $$\left( {\frac{1}{3} \times 12} \right){\text{ = 4 hrs}}$$ Since the leak empties one - third water, so time taken to fill the tank = Time taken by (A + B) to fill the whole tank + Time taken by (A + B) to fill one - third tank = (12 + 4) = 16 hours

q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 40 and 48 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minutes. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 30 minutes, The capacity of the tank is-
s: Work done by the waste pipe in 1 minute $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\frac{1}{{30}} - \left( {\frac{1}{{40}} + \frac{1}{{48}}} \right) \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{{30}} - \frac{{11}}{{220}}} \right) \\ & = - \frac{1}{{80}}\left[ { - \,{\text{Nagetive sign means emptying}}} \right] \\ & \therefore {\text{Volume of }}\frac{1}{{80}}{\text{ part = 3 galons}} \\ & {\text{Volume of whole tank}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {3 \times 80} \right){\text{gallons}} \\ & {\text{ = 240 gallons}}{\text{}} \end{aligned}$$

q: An outlet pipe can empty a cistern in 3 hours. In what time will empty $$\frac{2}{3}$$ of the cistern?
s: The outlet pipe empties the one complete cistern in 3 hours Time taken to empty $$\frac{2}{3}$$ Part of the cistern $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{= }}\frac{2}{3} \times 3 \\ & = 2\,{\text{hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A tank is 7 metre long and 4 meter wide wide. At what speed should water run through a pipe 5 cm broad and 4 cm deep so that in 6 hours and 18 minutes water level in the tank rises by 4.5 meter?
s: Rate of flow of water = x cm/minute ∴ Volume of water that flowed in the in 1 minutes = (5 × 4 × x) = 20 x cu.cm. ∴ Volume of water that flowed in the tank in 6 hours 18 minutes. i.e. (6 × 60 + 18) = 378 minutes = 2x × 378 cu. cm. According to question, $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{20}}x \times 378 = 700 \times 400 \times 450 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{700 \times 400 \times 450}}{{20 \times 378}}} \right){\text{cm /minutes}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{700 \times 400 \times 450 \times 60}}{{100000 \times 20 \times 378}}} \right){\text{km/hours}} \\ & \Rightarrow x{\text{ = 10 km/hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 16 hours respectively. A third pipe can empty the tank in 30 hours. If all three pipes are opened and functions simultaneously, how much time will the tank take to be full?( in hours )
s: First pipe fill the tank in 1 hour = $$\frac{1}{{12}}$$ part of tank Second pipe fill the tank in 1 hour = $$\frac{1}{{16}}$$ part of tank Third pipe empty the tank in 1 hour = $$\frac{1}{{30}}$$ part of tank When all three pipes are opened simultaneously, part of the tank filled in 1 hour $$= \frac{1}{{12}} + \frac{1}{{16}} - \frac{1}{{30}}$$ LCM of 12, 16 and 30 = 240 $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\frac{{20 + 15 - 8}}{{240}} \\ & = \frac{{27}}{{240}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required time taken by all the three pipes $${\text{ = }}\frac{{240}}{{27}} = \frac{{80}}{9} = 8\frac{8}{9}\,{\text{Hours}}$$

q: A tap can completely fill a water tank in 8 hours. The water tank has a hole in it through which the water leaks out. The leakage will cause the full water tank to get empty in 12 hours. How much time will it take for the tap the the tank completely with the hole?
s: Net part filled in 1 hour $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{{12}}} \right) = \frac{1}{{24}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ The tank will be filled in 24 hours

q: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 2 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. At 10 A.M. pipe A was opened. At what time will the tank be filled if pipe B is opened at 11 A.M. ?
s: Pipe A will fill 3 units till 11 A.M. Remaining capacity = 6 - 3 = 3 units Now both pipes will fill the tank in $$\frac{{{\text{Total Capacity}}}}{{{\text{Efficiency }}}} = \frac{3}{{\left( {3 + 1} \right)}} = \frac{3}{4}{\text{ hours}}$$ So, $$\left( {11 + \frac{3}{4}} \right)$$ A.M., tank will be filled = 11.45 A.M.

q: A water tank can be filled by a tap in 30 minutes and another tap can fill it in 60 minutes. If both taps are kept open for 5 minutes and then the first tap is closed, how long will it take foe the tank to be filled ?
s: (A + B)'s filling (2 + 1) = 3 units/min In 5 minutes they will fill 3 × 5 = 15 units Remaining capacity = 60 - 15 = 45 units Second pipe (B) fills it in $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{{\text{Remaining capacity}}}}{{{\text{efficiency of B}}}} \\ & = \frac{{45}}{1} \\ & = \,45\,{\text{minutes}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another can empty it in y hours. In how many hours they together fill it in ( y > x) ?
s: Time will be taken by both of them to fill the tank $${\text{ = }}\frac{{xy}}{{y - x}}$$

q: A water tap fills a tub in 'p' hours and a sink at the bottom empties it in 'q' hours. If p < q and both tap and sink are opened the tank is filled in 'r' hours, then the relation between p, q, r :
s: Net efficiency = q - p (n q > p) Time required $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{r}} = \frac{{pq}}{{q - p}} \\ & or\,\frac{1}{r} = \frac{1}{p} - \frac{1}{q} \end{aligned}$$

q: Three taps A, B, C can fill an overhead tank in 4, 6 and 12 hours respectively. How long would the three taps take to fill the tank if all of them are opened together ?
s: (A + B + C)'s efficiency = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units/hr (A + B + C) can fill the tank in $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\frac{{{\text{Total Capacity}}}}{{{\text{Efficiency of}}\left( {{\text{A + B + C}}} \right){\text{ }}}} \\ & = \frac{{12}}{6} \\ & = 2{\text{ hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Having the same capacity 9 taps fill up a water tank in 20 minutes. How many taps of the same capacity are required to fill up the same water tank in 15 minutes ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left[ {\frac{{{m_1} \times {h_1} \times {t_1}}}{{{w_1}}} = \frac{{{m_2} \times {h_2} \times {t_2}}}{{{w_2}}}} \right] \\ & {9_{taps}} \times {20_{\min }} = {t_{taps}} \times {15_{\min }} \\ & t = 12\,\,{\text{taps}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Pipe A can fill a tank in 4 hours and pipe B can fill it 6 hours. If they are opened on alternate hours and if pipe A is opened first then in how many hours, the tank shall be full ?
s: A → 4 hours B → 6 hours According to question, ⇒ For the first hour tap A is opened and B for second hour ⇒ Work done by both in 2 hours $$\begin{aligned} & \to \left( {3\,{\text{lit/h}} + 2\,{\text{lit/h}}} \right) \times 2 = 10\,{\text{units}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\mathop {\,\,|\,\,\, \times 2}\limits_{{\text{4 hours}}}^{{\text{2 hours}}} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\mathop {\,\,|\,\,\, \times 2}\limits_{{\text{10 litres}}}^{{\text{5 liters}}\,} \end{aligned}$$ ⇒ Remaining part = 12 - 10 = 2 liters ⇒ Again 5th hour A will be opened Tap A will fill the 2 liters water with its efficiency = $$\frac{2}{3}$$ hours ⇒ Therefore tank will be filled in = $$\left( {4 + \frac{2}{3}} \right)$$ hours = $${\text{4}}\frac{2}{3}$$ hours

q: Pipe A can fill the tank in 8 hours and pipe B can fill it in 12 hours. If pipe A is opened at 7:00 AM and pipe B is opened at 9:00 AM, then at what time will the tank be full ?
s: A opened 2 hours early to B In 2 hours A can do 3 × 2 = 6 unit work Remaining work = 24 - 6 = 18 A + B can do it in $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{18}}{5}{\text{hours}} \\ & = 3\frac{3}{5}{\text{hours}} \\ & {\text{ = 3}}\,{\text{hours 36 minutes}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Tank will be full in 9 AM + 3 hours 36 minutes = 12.36 PM

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank with water in 30 minutes and 45 minutes respectively. The third pipe C can empty the tank in 36 minutes. First A and B are opened. After 12 minutes C is opened. Total time ( in minutes ) in which the tank will be filled up is -
s: A . . . . . (+) 30 minutes B . . . . . (+) 45 minutes C . . . . . (-) 36 minutes ⇒ Water filled by (A + B) in 12 min = 12 × (6 + 4) = 12 × 10 = 120 liters ⇒ Remaining capacity = 180 - 120 = 60 liters ⇒ After 12 minutes emptied pipe C is also opened ⇒ Total capacity (A + B - C) = (6 + 4 - 5) = 5 liters/minutes ⇒ Time taken by (A + B - C) with capacity 5 liters/minutes to fill the remaining part $$= \frac{{60\,\,{\text{liters}}}}{{5\,\,{\text{liters/minutes}}}}{\text{ = 12 minutes}}$$ ⇒ Therefore, total time in which the tank will be filled up is = 12 + 12 = 24 minutes

q: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 6 hours, 9 hours and 12 hours respectively. B and C are opened for half an hour, then A is also opened. The time taken by the three pipes together to fill the remaining part of the tank is -
s: In half an hour (B + C) must have filled $$= \frac{4}{2} + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{7}{2}\,{\text{units}}$$ Capacity left $${\text{ = 36}} - \frac{7}{2} = \frac{{65}}{2}\,{\text{units}}$$ Now all pipes will fill the remaining tank $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\frac{{65}}{{2 \times \left( {6 + 4 + 3} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{65}}{{2 \times 13}} \\ & = \frac{5}{2} \\ & = 2\frac{1}{2}\,{\text{hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A tap drips at a rate of one drop/second. 600 drops make 100 ml. The number of liters wasted in 300 days is -
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{1 second }} \to {\text{ 1 drop}} \\ & {\text{Number of second in 300 days}} \\ & \left( {{{24}_{{\text{hrs}}}} \times {{60}_{{\text{mins}}}} \times {{60}_{{\text{sec}}}}} \right) \times 300\,{\text{days}} \\ & {\text{Number of milli - liters wasted}} \\ & {\text{100}} \times \frac{{24 \times 60 \times 60 \times 300}}{{600}} \\ & = 43200 \times 100 \\ & = 4320000\,{\text{ml}} \\ & = \frac{{4320000}}{{1000}} \\ & = 4320\,{\text{liters}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 15 minutes, respectively. The tank when fill can be emptied by pipe C in x minutes. When all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, the tank is full in 10 minutes. The value of x is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A + B + C = \frac{{60}}{{10}} \\ & 5 + 4 + C = 6 \\ & C = - 3 \\ & C{\text{ can empty the tank }}x \\ & = \frac{{60}}{3} = 20{\text{ minute}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A tap can fill a tank in $$5\frac{1}{2}$$ hours. Because of a leak, it took $$8\frac{1}{4}$$ hours to fill the tank. In how much time (in hours) will the leak alone empty 30% of the tank?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{I fill the tank}} = 5\frac{1}{2} = \frac{{11}}{2}{\text{ in hour}} \\ & {\text{I - II fill the tank}} = 8\frac{1}{4} = \frac{{33}}{4}{\text{ in hour}} \\ & {\text{LCM }}\left( {11,\,33} \right) = 33 \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Total work }}30\% = 33 \times \frac{{30}}{{100}} = \frac{{99}}{{10}} \\ & {\text{II}} = {\text{leak pipe efficiency}} = 6 - 4 = 2 \end{aligned}$$ Time taken by pipe to empty the tank = $$\frac{{99}}{{\frac{{10}}{2}}}$$ = $$\frac{{99}}{{20}}$$ in hour

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 24 minutes, respectively, while a third pipe C can empty the full tank in 32 minutes. All the three pipes are opened simultaneously. How-ever, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In how much time (in minutes) will the tank be full?
s: If pipe C continues for 2 more minutes, then = 2 × (-3) = -6 litre less fill Then, 96 - 6 = 90 litre filled A + B - C, 1 minute = 8 + 4 - 3 = 9 Time of A + B - C = $$\frac{{90}}{9}$$ = 10 minutes

q: A pump can fill a tank will water in 1 hour. Because of a leak, it took $$1\frac{1}{3}$$ hours to fill the tank. In how many hours can the leak alone drain all the water of the tank when it is full?
s: Let A and B are pipe and leakage B = 1 efficiently B = $$\frac{4}{1}$$ = 4 hrs

q: Pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 20, 30 and 60 hours, respectively. Pipes A, B and C are opened at 7 a.m., 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., respectively, on the same day. When will the tank be full?
s: Pipe A till 9 O'clock = 3 × 2 = 6 Pipe B till 9 O'clock = 2 × 1 = 2 Remaining work = 60 - 6 - 2 = 52 Time = $$\frac{{52}}{6}$$ = $$8\frac{4}{6}$$ = 8 hrs 40 min = 9:00 + 8 hrs 40 min = 05:40 pm

q: Pipes A and B are filling pipes while pipe C is an emptying pipe. A and B can fill a tank in 72 and 90 minutes respectively. When all the three pipes are opened together, the tank gets filled in 2 hours. A and B are opened together for 12 minutes, then closed and C is opened. The tank will be empty after:
s: A + B - C = 3 5 + 4 - C = 3 C = 6 In 12 min, (A + B) can fill = (5 + 4) × 12 = 9 × 12 The time was taken to empty (9 × 12) by 'C' Time $$= \frac{{9 \times 12}}{6} = 18\min$$

q: Two pipes A and B can fill cistern in $$12\frac{1}{2}$$ hours and 25 hours, respectively. The pipes were opened simultaneously, and it was found that, due to leakage in the bottom, it took one hour 40 minutes more to fill the cistern. It the cistern is full, in how much time (in hours) will the leak alone empty 70% of the cistern?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A = 12\frac{1}{2} = \frac{{25}}{2} \\ & B = 25 \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & A + B = \frac{{25}}{{2 + 1}} = \frac{{25}}{3} \\ & = 8\,{\text{hr }}20\,\min \\ & A + B - C \\ & = 8\,{\text{hr }}20\,\min + 1\,{\text{hr 4}}0\,\min \\ & = 10{\text{ hr}} \end{aligned}$$ C = 8 + 4 - 10 = 2 70% of tank capacity $$= 100 \times \frac{{70}}{{100}} = 70$$ Time taken in leakage $$= \frac{{70}}{2} = 35\,{\text{hrs}}$$

q: When operated separately pipe A takes 5 hours less than pipe B to fill a cistern, and when operated together, the cistern gets filled in 6 hours. In how much time (in hours) will pipe A fill the cistern, if operated separately?
s: \[\begin{array}{cccccccccccc} {\text{B}}&{}&{\text{A}} \\ {x + 5}&:&x \end{array}\] Now go through option, Let A = 10 hours B = 15 hours A + B = $$\frac{{30}}{5}$$ = 6 hours

q: The volume of a tank is 72 cubic metres. Water is poured into it at the rate of 60 litres per minute. How much time will it take to fill the tank?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & t = \frac{{7200}}{{60}}\min \\ & = 1200\min \\ & = \frac{{1200}}{{60}}{\text{ hours}} \\ & = 20{\text{ hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: 6 pipes, working 10 hours a day, can empty a cistern in 3 days. How many hours a day must 9 pipes work to empty the cistern in one day?

Tap A can fill a tank in 6 hours, tap B can fill the same tank in 8 hours and tap C can empty the same tank in 4 hours. If all three taps A, B and C are opened together, then how much time (in hours) will be taken to fill the tank?
s: Total work in a hours by (A + B + C) = 4 + 3 - 6 = 1 A + B + C = $$\frac{{24}}{1}$$ = 24 hours

q: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 hours and 15 hours respectively. Pipe C alone can empty the completely filled tank in 12 hours. First both pipes A and B are opened and after 5 hours pipe C is also opened. What is the total time (in hours) in which then tank will be filled?
s: According to question, Efficiency of (A + B) = 18 + 12 = 30 litre/hr In 5 hrs, filled capacity by (A + B) = 30 × 5 = 150 litres ∴ Remaining capacity = 180 - 150 = 30 litres Total efficiency of (A + B + C) = 18 + 12 - 15 = 15 litre/hr ∴ Time taken by (A + B + C) to fill the remaining capacity $$\Rightarrow \frac{{30}}{{15}} = 2\,{\text{hrs}}$$ ∴ Required time, to fill the complete tank = 5 hrs + 2 hrs = 7 hrs

q: Pipes A, B and C can fill a tank is 15, 30 and 40 hours, respectively. Pipes A, B and C are opened at 6 a.m., 8 a.m. and 10 a.m., respectively, on the same day. When will the tank be full?
Pipe A can fill the tank in 8 hours and pipe B can fill it in 12 hours. If pipe A is opened at 7:00 am and pipe B is opened at 9:00 am, then at what time will the tank be full?
s: A opened 2 hours early to B In 2 hours A can do 3 × 2 = 6 unit work Remaining work = 24 - 6 = 18 A + B can do it in $$\to \frac{{18}}{5}$$ = $$3\frac{3}{5}{\text{ hrs}}$$ = 3 hrs 36 min ∴ Tank will be full in 9 am + 3 hrs 36 min = 12 : 36 pm

q: Pipes A, B and C can fill an empty tank in $$\frac{{30}}{7}$$ hours, if all the three pipes are opened simultaneously. A and B are filling pipes and C is an emptying pipe. Pipe A can fill tank in 15 hours and pipe C can empty it in 12 hours. In how long (in hours) can pipe B alone fill the empty tank?

Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours, respectively, whereas pipe C and empty the full tank is 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe C is closed after 10 hours. After how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled?
s: All three pipe opened together in 10 hours = (15 + 10 - 6) × 10 = 190 Remaining work = 240 - 190 = 50 Remaining work done by A and B $$= \frac{{50}}{{15 + 10}} = 2$$

q: There are 3 taps, A, B and C, in a tank. These can fill the tank in 10 h, 20 h and 25 h, respectively. At first, all three taps are opened simultaneously. After 2 h, tap C is closed and tap A and B keep running. After 4 h, tap B is also closed. The remaining tank is filled by tap A alone. Find the percentage of work done by tap A itself.
s: C's work done in 2 hour = 4 × 2 = 8 B's work done in 4 hour = 5 × 4 = 20 A's share of work = 100 - 28 = 72

q: Pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 30h, 40h and 60h respectively. Pipes A, B and C are opened at 7 a.m., 8 a.m., and 10 a.m., respectively on the same day. When will the tank be full?

Pipes A and B can fill a tank in one hour and two hours respectively while pipe C can empty the filled up tank in one hour and fifteen minutes. A and C are turned on together at 9 a.m. After 2 hours. Only A is closed and B is turned on. When will the tank be emptied?
s: At 11 am, A is closed, now (B + C) will work together B + C = 5 - 8 = -3 The time was taken to fill 4 unit $$t = \frac{4}{3} = 1\frac{1}{3} = 1\,{\text{hr}}\,20\,\min$$

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in $$12\frac{1}{2}$$ hours and 25 hours, respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to a leakage in the bottom, it took 1 hour 40 minutes more to fill the cistern. When the cistern is full, in how much time will the leak empty the cistern?
s: Given: A can fill the cistern 12.5 hr B can fill the cistern 25 hr Formula Used: Total work = Efficiency × Time Calculation: Let the capacity of the cistern be 25 units (LCM of 12.5 and 25) ⇒ Efficiency of A = $$\frac{{25}}{{12.5}}$$ = 2 units/hr ⇒ Efficiency of B = $$\frac{{25}}{{25}}$$ = 1 units/hr ⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 2 + 1 = 3 units/hr Time taken by A and B to fill the cistern without leakage ⇒ $$\frac{{25}}{3}$$ = $$8\frac{1}{3}$$ hr = 8 hr 20 min Time taken by A and B to fill the cistern with leakage ⇒ 8 hr 20 min + 1 hr 40 min = 10 hr The combined efficiency of A and B with leakage ⇒ $$\frac{{25}}{{10}}$$ = 2.5 units/hr ⇒ Efficiency of leakage = 3 - 2.5 = 0.5 units/hr Time required by the leak to empty the full cistern ⇒ $$\frac{{25}}{{0.5}}$$ = 50 hr ∴ The leak can empty the full cistern in 50 hours.
